items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: the first drummer I ever seen, a solo drummer, was a drummer by the name of A.G. Godley

ctx.x: No, Alphonso Trent was actually, they were really ahead of their time. They were from, he’s from Arkansas, but he was rich, he was from this family that had plenty money and they had all kinds of uniforms, they were sharp looking cats, and they’d go in those white hotels and stay a year. They went in the Adolphus Hotel, where there were no blacks in © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -15-

those hotels, then they’d go to San Antonio, to the Gunter, and they appeared at all those hotels and things like that. So that’s why I always wanted to be with Trent, you know because of this, they had a good reputation and they never got stranded like bands were getting stranded there in those days, in big cars and all like that. Of course they had to take the freight elevator when they come to work, they’d look like the guests at the Adolphus Hotel, but when they got on that stand, the first drummer I ever…

He has a large picture of Alphonso Trent’s band. And I remember looking at these musicians, and he’s not one to brag, but he always said he had the sharpest band in the world, because they dressed, they had uniforms, and they were all good looking, very handsome men. And when we lived in Manhattan before we moved to Long Island, one of my girlfriends name was Joanie Cook and her father played for Trent, I mean for Alphonso. And I can remember thinking to myself when I was ten, I must have been around ten, he was…
